41848-with-the-jud-ans-in-the-palestine-.description: A book by Lieut.-Col. J. H. Patterson, D.S.O.. In the early days of 1917 the outlook for the Allied Powers was particularly black and menacing. England, the mainstay in the great struggle, was in deadly peril, for, just about this time, the ruthless Submarine campaign was at its height and our shipping losses were appalling.

arxiv-1606-02562.title: DialPort: Connecting the Spoken Dialog Research Community to Real User Data
arxiv-1606-02562.creator: Tiancheng Zhao Kyusong Lee Maxine Eskenazi
arxiv-1606-02562.description: Abstract This paper describes a new spoken dialog portal that connects systems produced by the spoken dialog academic research community and gives them access to real users. We introduce a distributed, multi-modal, multi-agent prototype dialog framework that affords easy integration with various remote resources, ranging from end-to-end dialog systems to external knowledge APIs.

arxiv-2202-02255.title: On the universality of fluctuations for the cover time
arxiv-2202-02255.creator: Nathanaël Berestycki, Jonathan Hermon, Lucas Teyssier
arxiv-2202-02255.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Nathanaël Berestycki, Jonathan Hermon, Lucas Teyssier. We consider random walks on finite vertex-transitive graphs Γ \Gamma of bounded degree. We find a simple geometric condition which characterises the cover time fluctuations: the renormalised cover time τ cov t hit − log ⁡ | Γ | \tfrac{\taucov}{\thit}-\log|\Gamma| converges to a standard Gumbel variable if and only if Diam ​ ( Γ ) 2 = o ⁡ ( n / log ⁡ n ) \mathrm{Diam}(\Gamma)^{2}=o(n/\log n) , where n = | Γ | n=|\Gamma| .

arxiv-2301-03579.title: Estimating the statistical uncertainty due to spatially correlated noise in interferometric images
arxiv-2301-03579.creator: Takafumi Tsukui, Satoru Iguchi, Ikki Mitsuhashi, Kenichi Tadaki
arxiv-2301-03579.description: Abstract Interferometers (e.g. ALMA and NOEMA) allow us to obtain the detailed brightness distribution of astronomical sources in 3 dimensions (R.A., Dec., frequency). However, the spatial correlation of the noise makes it difficult to evaluate the statistical uncertainty of the measured quantities and the statistical significance of the results obtained.

arxiv-2303-15398.title: Switching the Magnetization in Quantum Antiferromagnets
arxiv-2303-15398.creator: Katrin Bolsmann, Asliddin Khudoyberdiev, Götz S. Uhrig
arxiv-2303-15398.description: Abstract The orientation of the order parameter of quantum magnets can be used to store information in a dense and efficient way. Switching this order parameter corresponds to writing data. To understand how this can be done, we study a precessional reorientation of the sublattice magnetization in an (an)isotropic quantum antiferromagnet induced by an applied magnetic field.

arxiv-2311-07723.title: Generalization Analogies (GENIES): A Testbed for Generalizing AI Oversight to Hard-To-Measure Domains
arxiv-2311-07723.creator: Joshua Clymer, Garrett Baker, Rohan Subramani, Sam Wang
arxiv-2311-07723.description: Abstract As AI systems become more intelligent and their behavior becomes more challenging to assess, they may learn to game the flaws of human feedback instead of genuinely striving to follow instructions; however, this risk can be mitigated by controlling how LLMs generalize human feedback to situations where it is unreliable.

arxiv-2410-06559.title: The pseudometric topology induced by upper asymptotic density
arxiv-2410-06559.creator: Jonathan M. Keith
arxiv-2410-06559.description: Abstract . Upper asymptotic density induces a pseudometric on the power set of the natural numbers, with respect to which 𝒫 ⁡ ( ℕ ) {\mathcal{P}}({\mathbb{N}}) is complete. The collection 𝒟 {\mathcal{D}} of sets with asymptotic density is closed in this pseudometric, and closed subsets of 𝒟 {\mathcal{D}} are characterised by a generalisation of an additivity property (AP0).

arxiv-2501-11080.title: Below the Schwinger critical magnetic field value, quantum vacuum and gamma-ray bursts delay
arxiv-2501-11080.creator: Iver H. Brevik 1 , Moshe M. Chaichian 2 and Anca Tureanu 2
arxiv-2501-11080.description: Abstract A magnetic field above the Schwinger critical value B crit = 10 9 B_{\rm crit}=10^{9} Tesla is much higher than any magnetic field known by now in the interstellar bulk except in the vicinity of observed magnetars having magnetic fields between 10 9 10^{9} and 10 11 10^{11}~ Tesla.

arxiv-2504-12916.title: Exact Learning Dynamics of In-Context Learning in Linear Transformers and its application
arxiv-2504-12916.creator: Nischal Mainali, Lucas Teixeira
arxiv-2504-12916.description: Abstract Transformer models exhibit remarkable in-context learning (ICL), adapting to novel tasks from examples within their context, yet the underlying mechanisms remain largely mysterious. Here, we provide an exact analytical characterization of ICL emergence by deriving the closed-form stochastic gradient descent (SGD) dynamics for a simplified linear transformer performing regression tasks.

arxiv-2505-14902.title: RISC-Q: A Generator for Real-Time Quantum Control System-on-Chips Compatible with RISC-V
arxiv-2505-14902.creator: Junyi Liu, Yi Lee, Haowei Deng, Connor Clayton, Gengzhi Yang, Xiaodi Wu
arxiv-2505-14902.description: Abstract . Quantum computing imposes stringent requirements for the precise control of large-scale qubit systems, including, for example, microsecond-latency feedback and nanosecond-precision timing of gigahertz signals—demands that far exceed the capabilities of conventional real-time systems. The rapidly evolving and highly diverse nature of quantum control necessitates the development of specialized hardware accelerators.

arxiv-2507-18122.title: Maximizing Prefix-Confidence at Test-Time Efficiently Improves Mathematical Reasoning
arxiv-2507-18122.creator: Matthias Otth, Jonas Hübotter, Ido Hakimi, Andreas Krause
arxiv-2507-18122.description: Abstract Recent work has shown that language models can self-improve by maximizing their own confidence in their predictions, without relying on external verifiers or reward signals. In this work, we study the test-time scaling of language models for mathematical reasoning tasks, where the model’s own confidence is used to select the most promising attempts.

arxiv-2512-08741.title: Adaptive cut reveals multiscale complexity in networks
arxiv-2512-08741.creator: Louis Boucherie, Yong-Yeol Ahn, Sune Lehmann
arxiv-2512-08741.description: Abstract Hierarchical clustering and community detection are important problems in machine learning and complex network analysis. A common approach to identify clusters is to simply cut dendrograms at some threshold. However, single-level cuts are often suboptimal in terms of capturing underlying structure in the data, especially when the dendrogram is unbalanced.

pmc-11460944.title: Jonathan Yewdell Discusses Viral Immunology, Vaccine Development, Navigating a Scientific Career, and Offers Perspectives on Transforming Scientific Publishing and Research Education
pmc-11460944.creator: Neil S. Greenspan
pmc-11460944.description: In this interview, Jonathan Yewdell talks with Pathogens and Immunity senior editor Neil Green-span about the evolution of viral immunology, highlighting his work and the contributions of other influential scientists. He emphasizes the importance of passion and collaboration in scientific research, illustrating the potential for groundbreaking discoveries through networking.

pmc-11637238.title: Parvovirus B19 rebound outbreak 2024 and implications for blood‐ and plasma‐product safety
pmc-11637238.creator: Maria R Farcet, Michael Karbiener, Claudia Aberham, Nicholas Powers, Daniel Aue, Thomas R Kreil
pmc-11637238.description: BackgroundSince the beginning of 2024, several European countries reported unusually high numbers of Human parvovirus B19 (B19V) infections. An increase in B19V incidence rate might have implications for blood products for direct transfusion, however, large data sets for analysis of this outbreak are missing.

pmc-11676282.title: Impact of the Timed and Targeted Counselling Model on Maternal Health Continuum of Care Outcomes in Northern Uganda: Protocol of a Quasi-Experimental Study
pmc-11676282.creator: Douglas Zibugu, Jessica S. Gubbels, Christabellah Namugenyi, John Bosco Asiimwe, Sanne Gerards
pmc-11676282.description: Background: About 287,000 women died globally during their pregnancy journey in 2020, yet most of these deaths could have been prevented. In Uganda, studies show that using Community Health Worker (CHW) visits to households with a pregnant woman can support the prevention of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes.

pmc-12473969.title: Effects of After-School Basketball Program on Physical Fitness and Cardiometabolic Health in Prepubertal Boys
pmc-12473969.creator: Cristina Castro-Collado, Jose Manuel Jurado-Castro, Mercedes Gil-Campos, Belén Pastor-Villaescusa, Gracia María Quintana-Navarro, Francisco Jesús Llorente-Cantarero, Brendan O’Brien
pmc-12473969.description: Objectives: This study aimed to assess changes in anthropometric measures, cardiometabolic markers, and physical fitness following a structured basketball training program in healthy prepubertal boys. Methods: The intervention consisted of a 6-week pre-season phase followed by a 32-week basketball training season conducted during the academic year.

pmc-12616023.title: Dysregulation of apolipoprotein o reprograms CCR7+CD4+T cell fate in primary autoimmune thrombocytopenia
pmc-12616023.creator: Tengda Li, Xiang Li, He Huang
pmc-12616023.description: SummaryPrimary immune thrombocytopenia involves antibody-driven platelet loss and perturbed CD4+ T cell regulation. By integrating single-cell transcriptomic, epigenetic, and functional analyses, we delineated CCR7+CD4+ T cell states with distinct metabolic and transcriptional programs. A subset enriched in patients exhibited reduced oxidative phosphorylation and enhanced glycolysis, accompanied by elevated expression of SP100 and its downstream transcriptional targets FOXP1 and CDK6.

pmc-12743228.title: Pharmacist-Led Prevention of Recurrent Cetuximab Infusion Reactions
pmc-12743228.creator: Yota Yamada, Arisa Fukuyama, Motoyasu Miyazaki, Yasutaka Sumi, Haruka Fukue, Akio Nakashima, Takayuki Akasaki, Osamu Imakyure
pmc-12743228.description: Cetuximab infusion reactions (IRs) can disrupt the continuity of effective treatment. However, there is a lack of standardized practical ward-level strategies to prevent IR recurrence. Herein, we report a single-case observation of a pharmacist-led approach combining H2-receptor antagonist premedication with infusion-time extension in a high-risk patient.

pmc-13008548.creator: Toby Rogers, Vasilis C Babaliaros, Robert J Lederman, Jaffar M Khan, Adam B Greenbaum
pmc-13008548.description: tive multicenter studies and larger retrospective registries.1 Many of the more recent leaflet-modification techniques have not been subjected to similar scientific rigor. Then a balloon is inflated to create an orifice but not to completely tear the leaflet.

pmc-13044320.title: Dietary calcium citrate enhances nutrient digestibility and modulates cecal microbiota function in pre-laying hens
pmc-13044320.creator: Elena Yausheva, Tatiana Kholodilina, Elena Sizova, Daniil Shoshin, Kristina Ryazantseva, Ksenia Nechitailo, Tatiana Klimova, Alexandra Mustafina
pmc-13044320.description: Background and Aim:Calcium source and bioavailability are critical determinants of nutrient utilization, gut microbial ecology, and future productivity in laying hens, particularly during the pre-laying period. Organic calcium salts may exert additional functional effects through microbiota modulation beyond mineral supply alone.

pmc-13499858.title: Angiogenic Doping: Plausible Yet Difficult to Detect
pmc-13499858.creator: Sofie Lehto, Setareh Sima, Jaana Künnapuu, Sergei Iljukov, Michael Jeltsch
pmc-13499858.description: In endurance athletes, cardiovascular oxygen delivery is the primary limitation to performance. While the focus of athletes and regulatory bodies has been on hemoglobin and red blood cells, the increased oxygen-delivering capacity resulting from training is also a consequence of the expanded blood volume, which requires vascular adaptation.
